one_line: 15th‑century Adi Kabi of Odisha, village record‑keeper turned court‑linked poet of the Sarala Mahabharata.

appearance.age_look: early 40s, medium height, sturdy village-build with a calm yet energetic bearing
appearance.face: oval face with warm medium-brown Odia complexion, straight nose, slightly heavy brows, a short trimmed black beard and moustache, thoughtful almond-shaped eyes, and a gentle, introspective half-smile as default expression
appearance.hair: thick black hair pulled back into a small knotted bun at the back of the head, front kept neat with a slight wave, no shaving; a simple off-white cotton headband tied around the forehead, with a small vermilion tilak at the centre
appearance.costume: a 15th‑century Odia village‑scholar outfit: knee‑length off‑white handwoven cotton tunic (angarkha‑style opening slightly to the right, plain with subtle vertical weave texture), paired with a tightly wrapped cream dhoti with a thin maroon border reaching just above the ankles; over this, a soft turmeric‑yellow cotton uttariya shawl draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back, one end hanging in front; simple brown leather sandals; minimal jewellery—small round copper studs in the ears and a thin black cotton thread necklace with a tiny copper pendant tucked modestly under the tunic, hinting at village devotional practice
appearance.signature: a long palm‑leaf manuscript bundle tied with a dark brown cord in his left hand and a slender reed stylus held lightly between the fingers of his right hand, poised as if ready to write

ref_desc: Sarala Das appears as a sturdy early‑forties Odia man with an oval medium‑brown face, small bun and off‑white headband, in an off‑white tunic, cream dhoti, turmeric‑yellow shawl and sandals, carrying a palm‑leaf manuscript and reed stylus in warm cream and maroon tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of Sarala Das: a sturdy early‑forties Odia man with an oval medium‑brown face, thoughtful almond eyes, straight nose, slightly heavy brows, short trimmed beard and moustache, and a gentle introspective half‑smile. His thick black hair is pulled into a small knotted bun at the back, front neat with a slight wave, and he wears a simple off‑white cotton headband around his forehead with a small vermilion tilak at the centre. Dress him in a historically grounded 15th‑century Odia village‑scholar outfit: a knee‑length off‑white handwoven cotton tunic with an angarkha‑style opening slightly to the right and subtle vertical weave texture, a tightly wrapped cream dhoti with a thin maroon border reaching just above the ankles, and a soft turmeric‑yellow cotton uttariya shawl draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back, one end hanging in front. Add simple brown leather sandals, small round copper ear studs, and a thin black cotton thread necklace with a tiny copper pendant discreetly under the tunic. His signature props are a long palm‑leaf manuscript bundle tied with a dark brown cord in his left hand and a slender reed stylus held lightly in his right, as if ready to write. Use a warm palette of off‑white, cream, turmeric yellow, maroon, and brown, and present him in neutral, turn‑around poses that clearly show his face, hair, clothing details, and the manuscript and stylus from multiple angles.
